newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blast destroys house at Corsican golf course.
newsitem.headline: Blast destroys house at Corsican golf course.

text.p: Five armed and masked men burst into the house of a golf course keeper in Corsica on Thursday and blew it up with dynamite, a day after island separatists vowed to step up their struggle against France.

Police said the five men forced the keeper and two unidentified people who were with him to leave the house before placing the dynamite. The blast completely destroyed the house but nobody was injured.

No one claimed responsibility for the blast. The seaside golf course of Sperone has been hit by several blasts in the past, for which guerrillas of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility.

The FLNC, which took its bombing campaign to the French mainland in September, said in a statement on Wednesday it planned "new forms" of attacks on the mainland and threatened local politicians and the families of paramilitary police on the Mediterranean island.
"Since (Prime Minister Alain) Juppe has opted for a military solution...we have decided to adapt our struggle on the ground with increased resources," the FLNC's hardline "historic wing" said.
The FLNC claimed responsibility for a spectacular blast that wrecked Juppe's mayoral office in Bordeaux on October 5 as well as bombs in Marseille, Aix-en-Provence and Limoges last month.

The movement has always taken care to avoid civilian casualties but its threat added to the worries of police already on alert after a suspected Islamic fundamentalist bombing killed four people on a Paris underground train last week.
